data.narrative:
MatX is a Series B semiconductor company founded by Reiner Pope and Mike Gunter, having raised $500M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 8 private frontier-chip companies at similar or adjacent stages, alongside 3 public semiconductor peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) for sector context.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement to the $500M total raised proxy, implying a $950M valuation. Peer-median analysis across five same-sector comparables—SambaNova Systems ($11.0B, Series A), Etched ($5.0B, Series C), d-Matrix ($2.0B, Series C), Positron AI ($1.0B, Series B), and DEEPX ($529M, Series C)—yields a median of $2.0B, with a range of $529M to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied due to absence of MatX revenue disclosure, typical for private companies.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $808M to $2.3B, with a median of $1.5B across the two applicable methods. Key uncertainties center on MatX's current revenue run-rate and capital efficiency relative to peers, which would refine both the stage-progression and peer comparability assessments. The wide peer valuation dispersion ($529M–$11.0B) reflects heterogeneity in chip-sector positioning and burn profiles, underscoring reliance on operational metrics not present in this dataset.
